ky_crypt_the.blurb: The Crypt is a cluster of boulder problems in the Foxtown Boulders, set on a cliffline above two neighboring sectors with views out over the valley. Grades start at V1 and reach a single V10, but most of the problems fall between V1 and V4, so there is plenty for newer boulderers alongside a few serious tests. Expect flakes, arêtes and cracks, plus a traverse. The sector is a sunny one, which is welcome on cold days and less so in summer heat.
ky_crypt_the.parking_note: From Highway 89, turn onto Lime Kiln Ridge Road and bear right at the fork, then follow the dirt road for around two miles. Cars without four-wheel drive should stop at the first pullout and walk from there; capable 4WD vehicles can continue to the turnaround at the end of the service road. An upper and a lower lot serve the boulders.

ky_tower_rock.blurb: Tower Rock is a freestanding tower in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, within the Daniel Boone National Forest. The climbing is mostly traditional, with a handful of boulder problems as well. Grades run from easy fifth class up to a single 5.12, and the largest group sits in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. Caver's Route (5.3, trad) is the best known line, four pitches up a large fracture on the south end of the tower with a cave passage and a rappel to finish. Africa (5.9, trad), Arachnid (5.8+, trad) and Dog Days (5.8+, trad) are other good moderates.

ky_leonard_s_wall.blurb: Leonard's Wall is a small cliff band in the Bald Rock Recreational Preserve, tucked between Hazel Hollow and the back side of Velo crag. It offers a mix of sport and trad lines, and the grades are weighted toward 5.10, with a handful of 5.6 and 5.7 routes and a few 5.11s as well. Toe Beans (5.10a, sport) and Murder Mittens (5.10b, sport) are standouts at the middle grades, Leonard's Excellent Adventure (5.11a, sport) is a step up, and Pawsitively Purrfectly Meowvalous (5.7, trad) suits a warm-up.
ky_leonard_s_wall.approach: Follow the Hazel Hollow trail and bear right along the base. Where the wall turns to its front face, a path ascends through a rhododendron thicket to the first sport line, with the main stretch of cliff farther right.

ky_coopers_cove.blurb: Coopers Cove is a sunny, south-facing sport crag in the Miller Fork Recreational Preserve, with a good variety of slightly overhanging lines. Most of the routes fall between 5.10 and the low 5.12s, and the largest group is at 5.11, so it suits climbers working at that level. Shade is scarce, which makes it a good cold-weather choice and a hot one in summer. The Hustle (5.11b, sport), Addiction (5.11c, sport), Diesel Therapy (5.11a, sport) and Road Kill (5.10c/d, sport) are among the favorites.
ky_coopers_cove.approach: Cross the bridge over the creek and bear left onto the track that rejoins the road. Two roads on, turn left; then turn right at the second trail. It ends at Serenity Point, and the cliff base leads left to Coopers Cove, the next crag along.

ky_eastern_sky_bridge_ridge.blurb: Eastern Sky Bridge Ridge mixes older traditional classics with early sport testpieces, so it rewards a rack and a rope full of quickdraws alike. There are few easy lines here; most routes are 5.11 and 5.12, with a smaller group around 5.9 and 5.10 and a couple of boulder problems. The Underling (5.9, trad) is a good moderate, Inhibitor (5.11a, trad) is a wide-crack classic, and King Me (5.11b, sport) and Super Dario (5.11a, sport) are sport favorites. The walk in is short.
ky_eastern_sky_bridge_ridge.parking_note: Use the broad roadside pullout on KY 715 just beyond the concrete bridge, heading toward Pine Ridge, short of the Swift Camp trailhead lot across the road. Walk back toward the bridge to find the trail.

ky_funk_rock_city.blurb: Funk Rock City is a south-facing crag best known for technical, slabby lines in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with sport, trad and a top-rope option. Much of the rest of the wall runs through 5.12, with a few 5.13s. The wall soaks up sun, so it is a favorite in winter, provided the creek crossing on the way in is not running high. It feels wilder and quieter than many gorge cliffs. Prime Directive (5.11b, sport), The Infidel (5.11d, sport), Orange Juice (5.12c, sport) and Manic Impression (5.10a, sport) are the headliners.
ky_funk_rock_city.parking_note: Use the big pullout beside KY 715, roughly eight miles along from the Nada Tunnel end.

me_bald_bluff_bouldering.blurb: These are the boulder problems at Bald Bluff in western Maine, near the Mount Abram ski area. The rock is basalt, and the bouldering sits among caves and blocks beneath the cliffs. Grades run from VB up to V7, with most problems between V2 and V4, so it works for a range of abilities. The caves give steep, powerful climbing for people who would rather not rope up. The walk from the road is short, but it ends with a steady uphill stretch.
me_bald_bluff_bouldering.parking_note: Use the small pullout on Greenwood Road; it sits beside a guardrail whichever direction you arrive from.
